title: Chapter 12 — Industrial Training
description: Six months of industrial training in Lagos. Where you work decides who owns you, and one office has a secret about loan apps.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: SIWES: six months in a real Lagos office. A letter, a logbook, a supervisor's signature. Every student is scrambling for a placement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Expelled students don't get SIWES. But Mr. Effiong from PayWahala saw your akara spreadsheets online and doesn't care about letters. "Intern without a school," he calls you. It's a job.

options.text: Hon. Ronke's policy office in Ikeja.
options.lockedText: Ronke doesn't know you well enough

options.text: The Owó Ńlá Foundation office. They're your sponsors, after all.
PayWahala, a small fintech in Yaba. Mr. Effiong. No air conditioning.

beats.speaker: ronke
beats.text: You'll write the market sanitation brief. Real numbers. If they're wrong, I'll look stupid on television. Don't let me look stupid.

beats.objective: Survey the market toilets (or the lack of them). Talk to the traders.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You count three toilets for four thousand traders. One is locked. One is a store. One is a rumour.

beats.speaker: ronke
beats.text: (reading your brief) This is good. This is uncomfortable. (She signs your logbook.) Uncomfortable is the job.

beats.speaker: settlement
beats.text: Your duty: photographs. Every beneficiary must be photographed receiving their empowerment. Smiling. The generators, the sewing machines, the wheelbarrows.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You photograph forty sewing machines. On Monday, thirty-eight of them go back into the warehouse for next month's photographs.

options.text: Say nothing. Photograph the next batch.
Keep copies of the photos, with dates.

beats.speaker: effiong
beats.text: Somto. We build payment systems for market women. No loans. No harassment. (He gestures at three laptops and a fan.) Welcome to the future. It is hot.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You build a spreadsheet that tracks the akara economy of six bus stops. Mr. Effiong prints it out and sticks it on the wall like a painting.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Week ten. A client file lands on your desk by mistake: a data contract between a phone company and... QuickCash. The loan app. The one that called Mama.

variants.text: Week ten. A file on Barrister's desk: QuickCash's "community partnership". The loan app pays the Foundation. The Foundation gives it students' phone numbers. Yours was on the list.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: It's all here. Names, contacts, the scripts the collectors use.

options.text: Send it to Ifeoma Nwankwo at Wahala FM.
Close the file. Not your fight. You need the logbook signed.

beats.headline: Loan app shamed students with stolen contacts
beats.text: A source close to the data shows QuickCash bought students' phone books to shame borrowers. The app has "paused operations".

beats.title: Industrial Training
beats.summary: Six months in Lagos taught you more than three years of lectures: who owns what, who photographs whom, and where the phone numbers go.
